user: Is the deadline the same for every reason code?
answer:
No, the deadline differs by reason code. Each code has its own window, counted in days from the transaction date:

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

For TX-0401 (goods_not_received, 90 days), the window closes on **2026-10-18**, as noted earlier. A dispute filed after that date is not eligible. Also, a dispute filed under the wrong reason code is declined and must be refiled, which may push it past its window. So choosing the correct code matters.

Please confirm TX-0401, EUR 240.00, and goods not received, and I will open the dispute.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).

Reason code guide
## Choosing a code
The reason code must match what actually happened. A dispute filed under the
wrong code is declined and must be refiled, which may push it past its window.
